name: Visual Genome
description: Visual Genome is a dataset connecting language and vision using crowdsourced dense image annotations. It contains over 108,249 images, each annotated with an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships between objects. The dataset includes region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases are canonicalized to WordNet synsets. The dataset contains over 4.1 million objects, 1.6 million attributes, 1.8 million relationships, and 1.7 million question-answer pairs.
creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.-J., Shamma, D. A., Bernstein, M. S., & Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv:1602.07332.
rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT). The dataset was collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation. Approximately 800,000 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) were launched on AMT, where each HIT involved creating descriptions, questions and answers, or region graphs. Each HIT was designed such that workers could earn between $6-$8 per hour. The dataset uses 108,249 images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO, which are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images sourced from the intersection of YFCC100M (100 million Flickr images) and MS-COCO (328,000 images), resulting in 108,249 images. These are real-world, non-iconic images uploaded to Flickr by users. The images range from as small as 72 pixels wide to as large as 1280 pixels wide, with an average width of 500 pixels.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 6 months of data collection after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on data representation.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and question-answer pairs were canonicalized to WordNet synsets. Stanford NLP tools were used to extract noun phrases, which were then mapped to their most frequent matching synset in WordNet according to WordNet lexeme counts. Hand-crafted mapping rules were created for common failure cases (30 rules for objects, 15 for attributes, 20 for relationships). Attributes were normalized based on morphology (stemming). For relationships, prepositions were excluded and verb synsets were matched to WordNet sentence frames. All mappings were verified by AMT workers who confirmed or corrected the proposed synset mappings.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Region descriptions were preprocessed by removing all non-alphanumeric characters, lowercasing, and stripping excess whitespace. BLEU score thresholds (set to 0.7) were used to ensure diversity among descriptions. For objects, Stanford's dependency parser was used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions to workers. Bounding boxes were required to satisfy coverage (covering all mentioned objects) and quality (as tight as possible, relaxed to 4 pixels). Objects from different region graphs were merged if their bounding boxes had an overlap over union of 0.8, confirmed by workers. For attribute and relationship experiments, data was lowercased, lemmatized, and stripped of excess whitespace. For attribute prediction experiments, 500 attributes were randomly sampled from each category, with an 80%-10%-10% train/validation/test split.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were collected through multiple crowdsourcing stages on Amazon Mechanical Turk. For region descriptions: workers drew bounding boxes and wrote descriptions, with subsequent workers encouraged to write descriptions not previously written, enforced via BLEU score thresholds. For objects: workers extracted objects from descriptions and drew bounding boxes satisfying coverage and quality requirements. For attributes and relationships: workers added attributes to objects and connected pairs of objects with relationships based on region description text. For scene graphs: region graphs were combined by merging co-referenced objects (IoU >= 0.8), confirmed by workers. For QA pairs: workers wrote freeform QAs (8 pairs per image, at least 3 different W-types) and region-based QAs. All annotations went through verification using majority voting (3 workers, 2 must agree) or rapid judgments for objects. Canonicalization was verified by AMT workers who confirmed or corrected synset mappings from 5 options.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification was conducted using two strategies: majority voting (Snow et al., 2008) for all components except objects, and rapid judgments (Krishna et al., 2016) for objects. Majority voting involved three unique workers voting on each annotation, with an annotation accepted if at least two out of three workers verified it as correct. Canonicalization precision and recall were evaluated on randomly sampled held-out sets: Objects achieved 88.0% precision and 98.5% recall; Attributes achieved 85.7% precision and 95.9% recall; Relationships achieved 92.9% precision and 88.5% recall. The dataset achieved a 94.1% worker retention rate.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Average of 42 region descriptions per image, 21 objects per image, 16 attributes per image, 18 relationships per image, and 17 question-answer pairs per image. For verification, 3 workers per annotation item.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers contributed. Geographic distribution: United States 93.02%, Philippines 1.29%, Kenya 1.13%, India 0.94%, Russia 0.50%, Canada 0.47%, Others 2.65%. Age distribution: majority between 25 and 34 years old; youngest contributor was 18 years old, oldest was 68 years old. Gender distribution: 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser (Manning et al., 2014) was used to extract nouns automatically as suggestions for object extraction. Stanford NLP tools (Manning et al., 2014) were used to extract noun phrases from region descriptions and QAs for canonicalization. BLEU score (Papineni et al., 2002) was used programmatically to enforce diversity in region descriptions. word2vec (Mikolov et al., 2013) was used for semantic analysis of descriptions.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper refers to the dataset as 'the first release of the Visual Genome dataset' suggesting versioning is planned. The dataset is available online at https://visualgenome.org with API and additional information. No explicit deprecation policy or update schedule is described.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to enable cognitive computer vision tasks such as image description, question answering, and robotic interactions. It is intended to advance image search, question answering, and robotic interactions. The dataset could enable models that more thoroughly understand visual scenes, including the interactions and relationships between objects.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as the top synsets include humans playing sports. The image set shows a bias towards certain sports (skiing, surfboarding) which are overrepresented in attribute distributions. The geographic distribution of crowd workers is heavily skewed towards the United States (93.02%). Images were sourced from Flickr users, which may introduce biases related to the demographics of Flickr users and the types of images they upload.
rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are not perfect and still contain some ambiguity. The dataset's object categories (76,340 unique) result in lower per-category counts compared to datasets with fewer categories. Region descriptions have a maximum of 16 words. Some descriptions like 'it is a sunny day' contain no objects and therefore have no region graphs. The canonicalization of relationships excludes prepositions as they are not recognized by WordNet.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for: attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region description generation, visual question answering, dense image captioning, semantic image retrieval, object detection, scene graph generation, and image understanding evaluation. The dataset is designed as a general-purpose representation of the visual world without bias toward a particular task. It can be used for Training, Testing, and Validation.
